common.simulatedLong: Mock provider — simulated output, not an AI model
common.authorityTitle: No AI action runs without the configured authority mode
common.authorityNotice: Off sends nothing to any AI provider. Advisory only reads, analyses and drafts. Assisted runs an action only after a different, authorized person approves exactly the version shown. The AI can never approve gates or decisions, change baselines, budgets, ownership or permissions, grant data-room access, contact partners, sign, pay or declare closing — it can only prepare a request for the people who can.

modes.title: Authority modes
modes.hint: Each project has its own mode. Every tool and action is listed in the permission matrix; the server enforces the mode on every call.
modes.off: Platform and deterministic rules only. No data is sent to an AI provider.
modes.advisory: Authorized reading, analysis, recommendations and drafts. No approved-record changes and no messages. Default when AI is enabled.
modes.assisted: The AI prepares an action; it runs only after an authorized person approves exactly that version and content.
modes.autopilot: Only allowlisted low-impact internal actions under an approved policy with limits, scope, rate and expiry; revocable at once. Everything else needs approval.
modes.footer: Rules-only detections, the plan, the registers and the standard reports work in every mode, including Off.

proposals.title: AI proposals
proposals.subtitle: Actions the AI prepared. Nothing changes until a different authorized person approves exactly the version shown.
proposals.bindingNote: Approving binds the proposal version, its payload hash, the target record version and your identity. If anything changes afterwards, the server refuses the approval and a fresh review is needed.
proposals.modeNote: The project is in {mode} mode: proposals can be reviewed and rejected, but only Assisted or approved Autopilot mode lets an approved proposal run.
proposals.killSwitch: The emergency stop is active: approving and executing proposals is blocked, and pending proposals were cancelled (history is kept).
proposals.emptyHint: Proposals appear when the AI suggests a follow-up (for example in a briefing). Only proposals whose target you can see are listed.

proposal.simulatedNote: Prepared from Simulated mock output — not an AI model. Review it like any draft: it changes nothing unless an authorized person approves it.
proposal.bindingExplainer: Approving applies exactly version {version} with payload hash {hash} to the target at the version above. If the proposal is revised or the target record changes, the server refuses a stale approval.
proposal.noUnderlying: None — text for a person only
proposal.sodNote: Separation of duties: the person on whose behalf the AI prepared a proposal cannot approve it; the approver must also hold the permission the action exercises. The server enforces both.

approveBlocked.noPermission: You can review this proposal; approving needs the proposal-approval permission.
approveBlocked.notExecutable: This is a prepared request for a person; it can never be executed.
approveBlocked.selfApproval: You cannot approve this proposal: it was prepared on your behalf. A different authorized person must approve it (separation of duties).
approveBlocked.noAuthority: You cannot approve this proposal: executing it exercises {permission}, which you do not hold.
approveBlocked.notPending: Only a proposal awaiting review can be approved (this one is {status}).
approveBlocked.killSwitch: Approving is blocked while the emergency stop is active.
approveBlocked.mode: Approving is not available in {mode} mode: proposals run only in Assisted or approved Autopilot mode.

proposal.approveC1: Your approval is bound to proposal version {version} and payload hash {hash}.
proposal.approveC2: It is also bound to the target {target} at version {version}; if the record changes first, the approval is refused.
proposal.approveC2none: The proposal has no target record.
proposal.approveC3: The approval is single-use and valid for 24 hours. The worker executes it after re-checking the mode, the emergency stop and everyone's permissions.
proposal.approveC4: Messages are in-app only; e-mail, Teams and SMS stay disabled.
proposal.approveC5: The recipient must be allowed to read the target and every source the AI used to draft this message. The server checks this now and again just before sending, and refuses otherwise.
proposal.boundTo: Bound to proposal version {version}. A different current version is refused by the server.
proposal.approved: Proposal approved — the worker will execute it.
proposal.rejectC1: The proposal will not run; any valid approval is invalidated.
proposal.rejectC2: Your reason is recorded in the proposal history.
proposal.reviseC1: The payload changes, so its hash changes and a new proposal version is created.
proposal.reviseC2: Existing approvals are invalidated; a different person must review the new version.
proposal.reviseC3: The recipient and target stay the same and are checked again by the server.
proposal.revised: Proposal revised — a fresh review is needed.

reasons.target_version_changed: the target record changed after the proposal was prepared
reasons.recipient_not_cleared_for_content: the recipient may not read every source the AI used to draft the message
reasons.recipient_not_authorized: the recipient is not an authorized internal member of the project for this record
reasons.recipient_no_longer_authorized: the recipient is no longer an authorized internal member of the project for this record
reasons.requester_not_cleared_for_content: the person it was prepared for may no longer read its target or every source the AI used
reasons.requester_no_longer_authorized: the person it was prepared for no longer holds the required permission

briefings.delivery: Each briefing is generated under your own access and delivered to you only. It is skipped, and nothing is sent, if you lose access or AI is Off.
briefings.emptyHint: Subscribe below to receive a daily briefing or a weekly summary.
briefings.cronHint: Five-field cron. Leave empty for the default ({cron}).

settings.title: AI settings & controls
settings.subtitle: Authority mode, provider, budgets and schedule for this project; the autopilot policy; and the emergency stop.
settings.notManager: Changing the mode, provider and budgets needs the AI settings permission. Your role may still use the emergency stop below if it is offered.
settings.formHint: Saving is a single versioned change: you review the exact differences first, and the server refuses it if someone else changed the settings meanwhile.
settings.providerHint: Each option shows the status the server reports. A provider whose endpoint is not configured or not approved cannot be selected — the server refuses it.
settings.modelHint: For the mock: mock-benign. Leave empty for the provider default.
settings.ceiling: Highest classification sent to the provider
settings.ceilingHint: Content above this is withheld. The provider's own hard limit also applies; strictly confidential, partner-room and clean-team content is never sent.
settings.monthlyTokenBudgetHint: Required to enable AI. When it is used up, AI pauses; project management does not.
settings.perRunTimeoutHint: Questions answered while you wait are capped at 25 seconds.
settings.quietHint: Messages are deferred until the end of the quiet window.
settings.briefingCronHint: Five-field cron; also updates your own daily briefing.
settings.enableConsequence: AI becomes active for this project in the selected mode; questions and briefings send authorized, classification-limited context to the selected provider.
settings.saveConsequence: The change is recorded in the audit history with your reason.
settings.boundTo: Based on settings version {version}. A different current version is refused by the server.

errors.budgetRequired: Set a monthly token budget above zero before enabling AI.
errors.range: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
errors.decimal: Enter an amount with at most 4 decimal places.
errors.currency: Use a three-letter ISO 4217 code (for example SAR).
errors.currencyRequired: A cost budget needs a currency.
errors.providerRequired: A mode other than Off needs a provider.

autopilot.title: Autopilot policy
autopilot.hint: Proposed here by a settings administrator and approved by a different person. Only allowlisted low-impact actions, with a daily limit and an expiry of at most 90 days. Revoking takes effect at once and returns the mode to Assisted.
autopilot.allowlistHint: Only these low-impact internal actions are eligible.
autopilot.none: No autopilot policy. Autopilot mode cannot be selected without an approved policy.
autopilot.approveNeedsPermission: Approving the policy needs the autopilot-approval permission.
autopilot.selfApproval: You proposed this policy, so you cannot approve it. A different person with the autopilot-approval permission must approve it (enforced by the server).
autopilot.proposeC1: The policy is only proposed; it does nothing until a different authorized person approves it.
autopilot.proposeC2: A new proposal replaces any existing policy and needs a fresh approval.
autopilot.proposeC3: Autopilot mode can be selected only after approval.
autopilot.proposed: Autopilot policy proposed — it needs a different person's approval.
autopilot.approveC1: The allowlisted actions may then run without a per-action approval, within the daily limit and until the expiry date.
autopilot.approveC2: Everything else still needs a human approval; the policy can be revoked at any time.
autopilot.revokeC1: No further action runs under the policy.
autopilot.revokeC2: If the mode is Autopilot, it drops to Assisted immediately.

killSwitch.title: Emergency stop
killSwitch.hint: Stops all AI work in this project at once. History is preserved.
killSwitch.stateUnknown: The emergency-stop state is shown to holders of the run-read or settings permission.
killSwitch.bannerBody: Asking, approving and executing are blocked; queued AI work, pending proposals and unsent AI messages were cancelled. History is preserved.
killSwitch.selfRelease: You activated the emergency stop, so you cannot release it. A different authorized person must release it (enforced by the server).
killSwitch.releaseNeedsPermission: Releasing needs the release permission and must be done by someone other than the person who activated it.
killSwitch.activateC1: New questions and briefings are refused immediately.
killSwitch.activateC2: Queued AI jobs are cancelled; valid approvals are invalidated and pending proposals are cancelled.
killSwitch.activateC3: Unsent AI messages are cancelled. Messages already delivered cannot be recalled.
killSwitch.activateC4: All history is kept. Only a different authorized person can release the stop.
killSwitch.activated: Emergency stop active: {jobs} jobs cancelled, {approvals} approvals invalidated, {proposals} proposals cancelled, {deliveries} messages cancelled.
killSwitch.releaseC1: AI work may resume in the configured authority mode.
killSwitch.releaseC2: Cancelled proposals and jobs stay cancelled; new work starts fresh.
killSwitch.sod: Separation of duties: the person who activated the stop cannot release it.

ai.ceiling_exceeds_provider_limit: The classification ceiling is above what this provider may receive.

ai.cost_currency_required: A cost budget needs a currency.
